scenario: [LADP.3.1.1] / [LADP.3.2.1] (LADP.11.3, the id, and LADP.11.2 are tombstones): an adapter entity set is written as a regex the author puts over the identity slot, not as a dotted pattern sugar or a grammar wildcard. `[^.]*` stands for "any run within one entity_id segment". The rule `motion` matches `BinarySensor b where b.entity_id ~ /^binary_sensor\.[^.]*_motion$/ and b.state == true`. Three sensors, all `state: true`, one pump each: `binary_sensor.hall_motion` fires; `binary_sensor.hall_door` does not (wrong suffix); `binary_sensor.a.b_motion` does not, because `[^.]*` stops at a dot, as a segment glob would. One message, the matching entity_id. A runtime that matched the regex unanchored, or let `.` in the pattern match anything but a literal dot, logs more.
rules_ds:
schema BinarySensor scope logical:
    entity_id: String key
    state: Bool mutable

rule motion:
    BinarySensor b where b.entity_id ~ /^binary_sensor\.[^.]*_motion$/ and b.state == true
->
    log info "{b.entity_id}"
